name: Financial Accounting
topics: Nature, users and concepts of accounting
Source documents and books of original entry
Trial balance and correction of errors
Petty cash book and the imprest system
Final accounts of a sole trader
Adjustments: accruals, prepayments, bad debts and provisions

questions.q: Which of the following best describes accounting as a discipline practised by a book-keeper like Mrs. Nkechi in her provision store at Onitsha?
o: The process of recording only the cash transactions of a business
The process of checking financial statements for fraud after they are prepared
The act of preparing tax returns for government agencies
The process of identifying, recording, classifying and summarising financial transactions to provide information for decision making
questions.e: Accounting is defined as the process of identifying, recording, classifying, summarising and interpreting financial transactions to give useful information to users. The other options describe only a narrow part of accounting work, not the full discipline.
questions.p: Accounting na the process wey dem dey identify, record, classify and summarise money matter for business so dat people fit use am take decision. The other options na small small part of the work, dem no cover the whole thing.

questions.q: Hassan Textiles Ltd wants to borrow ₦2,000,000 from First Trust Bank to expand its shop in Kano. Before granting the loan, the bank studies the company's financial statements. In this situation, First Trust Bank is acting as what type of user of accounting information?
questions.e: External users are people outside the day-to-day running of the business who use its financial statements, such as banks, suppliers and investors. The bank is not part of Hassan Textiles' management, so it is an external user assessing credit worthiness.
questions.p: External user na person wey no dey inside the company management but still dey use the account to take decision, like bank, supplier or investor. Since the bank no be staff of Hassan Textiles, dem be external user wey wan check if the company fit pay back loan.

questions.q: Which accounting concept assumes that a business, such as Obi Stores in Enugu, will continue to operate for the foreseeable future and will not be forced to close down or sell off its assets suddenly?
questions.e: The going concern concept assumes a business will continue operating into the foreseeable future, which is why assets are valued at cost rather than forced-sale (liquidation) value. Prudence, materiality and realisation deal with other accounting matters, not business continuity.
questions.p: Going concern concept na the idea say the business go continue to dey run well well for future, e no go just close down sharp sharp. Na why dem dey value asset for normal price, no be quick-quick sale price. The other options no concern business continuity.

questions.q: Chidinma's Fashion House pays rent of ₦60,000 in December 2023 to cover the months of January, February and March 2024. Which accounting concept requires that this ₦60,000 be treated as a prepayment and charged as an expense in the 2024 financial year, not in 2023?
questions.e: The matching (accrual) concept states that expenses should be recognised in the period they relate to, not necessarily when cash is paid. Since the rent covers 2024, it must be matched against 2024's income, not 2023's, so it is shown as a prepayment in 2023.
questions.p: Matching concept talk say expense suppose dey record for the period wey e concern, no be the period wey dem pay the cash. Since the rent na for 2024, dem go record am as prepayment for 2023 account, no be as expense for 2023.

questions.q: For five years, Danjuma Ventures used the straight-line method to depreciate its delivery van. In the sixth year, without any disclosure in the notes to the accounts, the business suddenly switched to the reducing balance method. This action goes against which accounting concept?
questions.e: The consistency concept requires that once an accounting method is adopted, it should be applied the same way from one period to another, and any change should be disclosed. Changing the depreciation method without disclosure breaks this rule, making comparison of accounts difficult.
questions.p: Consistency concept talk say once business choose one method, dem suppose dey use am every year, and if dem wan change am, dem must talk am for the notes. Since Danjuma Ventures change am just like that without explanation, e don break consistency concept.

questions.q: At the end of the year, Mr. Eze's inventory of rice cost him ₦150,000 to buy, but because of a sudden fall in market price, it can now only be sold for ₦120,000. According to the prudence concept, at what value should this inventory be shown in the financial statements?
questions.e: The prudence concept requires inventory to be valued at the lower of cost or net realisable value, so losses are not overstated as profit. Here, cost is ₦150,000 but net realisable value is ₦120,000, so the lower figure, ₦120,000, is used.
questions.p: Prudence concept talk say dem suppose value inventory with whichever one dey lower between cost and the price wey e fit sell. Cost na ₦150,000 but the sell price don fall reach ₦120,000, so dem go use ₦120,000 wey be the smaller one.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa owns a provisions business. One day he withdraws ₦50,000 from the business bank account to pay his daughter's school fees. Which accounting concept requires that this withdrawal be recorded as drawings in the business books and not treated as a business expense?
questions.e: The business entity concept treats the business as separate from its owner, so the owner's personal spending, like school fees, is not a business expense but drawings from the owner's capital. This keeps the business's own financial position accurate and separate from Alhaji Musa's personal affairs.
questions.p: Business entity concept dey separate the business from the owner, so wetin the owner spend for im personal matter, like school fees, no be business expense; na drawings from im capital. This one dey make sure say the business account no mix up with the owner personal money.

questions.q: A trader sold goods on credit to a customer. Which source document will the trader prepare and send to the customer, showing the quantity, description, unit price and total amount of the goods sold?
questions.e: An invoice is the source document a seller issues to a buyer for goods sold on credit. It shows quantity, price, trade discount and total amount owed.
questions.p: Invoice na di paper wey seller dey write give buyer wen e sell goods on credit. E go show di quantity, price and di total money wey buyer go pay.

questions.q: Which of the following source documents is used to acknowledge that cash or cheque has been received from a customer in settlement of a debt?
questions.e: A receipt is issued by the person receiving money to confirm that payment (cash or cheque) has been received from the payer.
questions.p: Receipt na di document wey di person wey collect money dey give to show say e don receive di money from di person wey pay.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa sold goods worth ₦30,000 on credit to Mrs Chioma. Mrs Chioma later returned goods worth ₦4,000 because they were the wrong size. Which document will Alhaji Musa send to Mrs Chioma to reduce the amount she owes?
questions.e: A credit note is issued by the seller to reduce a customer's debt when goods are returned or an overcharge is corrected. Here, Alhaji Musa (seller) reduces Mrs Chioma's balance by ₦4,000.
questions.p: Credit note na wetin seller dey use reduce di money wey customer owe am wen customer return goods. Na Alhaji Musa go send am give Mrs Chioma to reduce her debt by ₦4,000.

questions.q: A supplier's invoice to Bayo Stores understated the price of some goods supplied, so the total amount charged was less than the correct amount. Which document will the supplier send to Bayo Stores to correct this error and increase the amount owed?
questions.e: A debit note is sent when an amount owed needs to be increased, such as when an invoice was undercharged. It informs the buyer that more money is now owed.
questions.p: Debit note na wetin dem dey use when di money wey person owe need increase, like wen invoice no charge well. E go tell Bayo Stores say dem owe more money now.

questions.q: Which book of original entry is used to record credit purchases of goods bought for resale, before the entries are posted to the individual suppliers' accounts in the purchases ledger?
questions.e: The purchases day book (purchases journal) records all credit purchases of goods meant for resale, using details from suppliers' invoices, before posting to the purchases ledger.
questions.p: Purchases day book na where dem dey first write credit purchases of goods wey business buy to resell, before dem post am go di purchases ledger.

questions.q: Chief Okafor's petty cashier operates an imprest system with a fixed float of ₦15,000. During the week, the following payments were made from petty cash: stationery ₦2,300, transport ₦3,750, postage stamps ₦1,450, and refreshment for staff ₦2,000. How much will the chief cashier reimburse the petty cashier at the end of the week to restore the imprest to its original level?
questions.e: Under the imprest system, reimbursement equals total expenses paid out, not the balance remaining. Total expenses = 2,300+3,750+1,450+2,000 = ₦9,500, so this amount restores the float to ₦15,000.
questions.p: For imprest system, dem go only refund di total money wey petty cashier don spend. Total spend = 2,300+3,750+1,450+2,000 = ₦9,500, so na dat money dem go give am back make di float reach ₦15,000 again.

questions.q: Golden Enterprises received an invoice of ₦68,000 for goods bought on credit from Zenith Traders. Golden Enterprises later returned damaged goods worth ₦12,000 to Zenith Traders and received a credit note for this amount. What is the net amount Golden Enterprises will finally pay to Zenith Traders for this transaction?
questions.e: A credit note reduces the amount a buyer owes when goods are returned. Net amount payable = ₦68,000 (invoice) minus ₦12,000 (credit note) = ₦56,000.
questions.p: Credit note dey reduce di money wey buyer owe wen e return goods. So di net money wey Golden Enterprises go pay = ₦68,000 minus ₦12,000 = ₦56,000.

questions.q: In double entry bookkeeping, when a trader in Onitsha buys goods worth ₦20,000 for cash, which entry is correct?
o: Debit Cash account, Credit Sales account
Debit Purchases account, Credit Cash account
Debit Cash account, Credit Purchases account
Debit Sales account, Credit Cash account
questions.e: Purchases is an expense/asset coming into the business, so it is debited. Cash is going out, so it is credited. This follows the rule: debit what comes in, credit what goes out.
questions.p: Purchases na something wey enter business so dem go debit am. Cash dey comot so dem go credit am. Na the rule be that - debit wetin enter, credit wetin comot.

questions.q: The book of account that contains all the individual accounts (personal, real and nominal) of a business is called the?
questions.e: The ledger is the principal book of accounts where all transactions are classified and recorded under separate accounts. The journal only records transactions before posting, while the trial balance is a list of balances, not a book of accounts.
questions.p: Ledger na the main book wey get all the accounts (personal, real and nominal) wey business use record transactions. Journal na where dem first write am before dem post am go ledger, trial balance na just list of balances.

questions.q: Which of the following is a personal account in the ledger of a business?
questions.e: Personal accounts relate to individuals, firms or organisations, such as Chidi, who owes the business money as a debtor. Rent and Sales are nominal accounts while Furniture is a real account.
questions.p: Personal account na account wey concern person, company or organisation, like Chidi wey owe business money as debtor. Rent and Sales na nominal accounts, Furniture na real account.

questions.q: In the ledger, an increase in a liability account, such as a Loan account, is normally recorded on which side?
questions.e: Liabilities increase on the credit side and decrease on the debit side, following the double entry rule for liabilities. A loan received increases what the business owes, so it is credited.
questions.p: Liability dey increase for credit side and e dey reduce for debit side, na so double entry rule take be for liability. If business collect loan, wetin e owe increase, so dem go credit am.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the golden rule applied to a real account (such as Furniture or Motor Vehicle account) in double entry bookkeeping?
o: Debit the receiver, credit the giver
Debit all expenses, credit all incomes
Debit what comes in, credit what goes out
Debit the giver, credit the receiver
questions.e: Real accounts deal with assets, so the rule is to debit what comes into the business and credit what goes out. The rule about receiver and giver applies to personal accounts, while expenses and incomes apply to nominal accounts.
questions.p: Real account na about assets, so the rule be say debit wetin enter business and credit wetin comot. The receiver and giver rule na for personal account, expenses and incomes na for nominal account.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a trial balance in financial accounting?
o: A list of ledger account balances extracted to check the arithmetical accuracy of the books
A statement showing the profit or loss made by a business during a trading period
A summary of all cash transactions during an accounting period
A statement showing the financial position of a business at a particular date
questions.e: A trial balance is a list of all ledger balances (debit and credit) drawn up to test whether the double entry has been correctly done. It is not the same as a balance sheet or a profit and loss account.
questions.p: Trial balance na list of all the ledger balances wey dem bring together to check if the double entry correct well. E no be balance sheet or profit and loss account.

questions.q: Adaeze, a trader, forgot to record a cash sale of ₦12,000 in both the Sales account and the Cash account. What type of error has occurred?
questions.e: Since the transaction was not entered anywhere at all (no debit and no credit), it is an error of complete omission. This type of error does not affect the trial balance agreement because both sides are equally unaffected.
questions.p: Since dem no enter the transaction for any account at all, na error of complete omission. This kind error no go affect trial balance agreement because both sides no get wetin enter.

questions.q: Chief Obi's draft trading and profit and loss account showed a net profit of ₦240,000. It was later discovered that a credit purchase of goods worth ₦18,000 had been completely omitted from the books. After correcting this error, what is the correct net profit?
questions.e: Omitting a credit purchase means purchases (and cost of sales) were understated by ₦18,000, which made net profit overstated. Correct net profit = ₦240,000 - ₦18,000 = ₦222,000.
questions.p: If dem miss credit purchase, e mean say purchases and cost of sales dey less by ₦18,000, so profit go too high. Correct profit = ₦240,000 - ₦18,000 = ₦222,000.

questions.q: A trader bought a delivery van for ₦850,000 for his transport business but debited the full amount to the Motor Running Expenses account instead of the Motor Vehicle (fixed asset) account. What type of error is this?
questions.e: Treating a capital expenditure (purchase of a fixed asset) as a revenue expense breaks the basic accounting principle of distinguishing capital from revenue items, so it is an error of principle. The trial balance will still balance because a debit entry was still made, just in the wrong class of account.
questions.p: To treat capital spending (buying asset) as if na revenue expense dey break basic accounting principle, so na error of principle. Trial balance go still balance because debit entry still dey, na wrong class of account dem use.

questions.q: An accounting clerk recorded a cash payment of ₦7,500 made to a supplier, Mr. Bala, by debiting the Cash account and crediting Bala's account — a complete reversal of the correct entries. What amount should be used in the journal entry to correct this error?
questions.e: To correct a complete reversal, you must first cancel the wrong entry (₦7,500) and then record the correct entry (another ₦7,500), giving a total correcting amount of 2 x ₦7,500 = ₦15,000, debited to Bala's account and credited to Cash.
questions.p: To correct complete reversal, you go first cancel the wrong entry (₦7,500) then do the correct entry (another ₦7,500) — altogether na 2 x ₦7,500 = ₦15,000, wey go debit Bala account and credit Cash.

questions.q: What is the main purpose of a cash book in a business?
o: To summarise the fixed assets of the business
To record all cash and bank transactions as they occur
To record only transactions on credit
questions.e: The cash book is a book of original entry that records all cash and bank receipts and payments in order of date. It also serves as a ledger account for cash and bank.
questions.p: Cash book na book wey dem dey use record all cash and bank money wey enter or comot, as e dey happen. E dey also serve as ledger for cash and bank.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT usually found as a column in a three-column cash book?
questions.e: A three-column cash book has discount, cash and bank columns on both the debit and credit sides. Sales are recorded in the sales day book or sales ledger, not directly as a cash book column.
questions.p: Three-column cash book get discount, cash and bank columns for both sides. Sales no be column for cash book, na for sales day book or sales ledger.

questions.q: Mrs. Chukwu's cash book showed a debit balance of ₦45,000 at the start of the month. During the month, she recorded cash sales of ₦120,000 and cash purchases of ₦85,000 directly in the cash book, with no other transactions. What is the closing balance of the cash book?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + Receipts - Payments = 45,000 + 120,000 - 85,000 = ₦80,000.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + wetin enter - wetin comot = 45,000 + 120,000 - 85,000 = ₦80,000.

questions.q: A cheque that has been issued by a business and recorded in the cash book, but which has not yet been presented at the bank for payment, is known as a/an:
questions.e: An unpresented cheque is one already written out and entered in the cash book by the business but which the receiver has not yet taken to the bank for payment, so it does not yet appear on the bank statement.
questions.p: Unpresented cheque na cheque wey business don write and enter for cash book, but the person wey carry am never go bank collect money, so e never show for bank statement.

questions.q: When a business owner withdraws ₦10,000 cash from the bank for office use, this is entered on the debit side of the cash column and the credit side of the bank column of the same cash book, on the same date. This type of entry is called:
questions.e: A contra entry occurs when a transaction affects both the cash and bank columns of the same cash book, such as withdrawing cash from the bank or paying cash into the bank. It is marked with a 'C' in the folio column.
questions.p: Contra entry na when one transaction touch both cash and bank columns for the same cash book, like when you comot cash from bank or pay cash enter bank. Dem dey mark am with letter 'C' for folio column.

questions.q: The bank column of Alhaji Musa's cash book showed a debit balance of ₦60,000 on 30th June. On comparing it with the bank statement, it was found that: a cheque of ₦8,000 issued to a supplier had not yet been presented; a cheque of ₦15,000 paid into the bank had not yet been credited; the bank had credited interest of ₦1,000 not yet recorded in the cash book; and the bank had charged ₦500 commission not yet recorded in the cash book. What is the adjusted cash book balance?
questions.e: Only items missing from the cash book (bank interest and bank charges) are used to adjust it; unpresented cheques and uncredited lodgements only affect the bank statement side. Adjusted balance = 60,000 + 1,000 - 500 = ₦60,500.
questions.p: Na only the items wey never dey for cash book (bank interest and bank charges) dem go use adjust am; unpresented cheque and uncredited lodgement na for bank statement side. Adjusted balance = 60,000 + 1,000 - 500 = ₦60,500.

questions.q: In the imprest system of petty cash, the petty cashier is given a fixed sum of money at the start of each period. This fixed sum is called the:
questions.e: Under the imprest system, the petty cashier always starts a new period with the same fixed amount of cash, known as the float. This amount is topped up at the end of each period to restore it to the fixed level.
questions.p: For imprest system, dem go always give the petty cashier the same fixed amount wey dem dey call float at the start of every period. Dem go top am up again make e reach that same level.

questions.q: Which of these best explains why a business keeps a petty cash book?
o: To record large capital expenditure such as purchase of a delivery van
To prepare the statement of financial position of the business
To calculate the net profit of the business
To record small, day-to-day cash expenses separately from the main cash book
questions.e: A petty cash book is kept to record small, routine cash payments like stationery, postage and transport fares, so that the main cash book is not cluttered with minor entries.
questions.p: Petty cash book na for record small small cash wey dem dey spend every day like stationery, postage and transport, so that main cash book no go too full with small small entries.

questions.q: Adaeze Ventures operates the imprest system with a petty cash float of ₦15,000. During the month, the petty cashier spent ₦4,200 on stationery, ₦3,100 on postage and ₦2,700 on cleaning materials. How much will the head cashier give the petty cashier at the end of the month to restore the float to its original level?
questions.e: Total expenses for the month = 4,200 + 3,100 + 2,700 = ₦10,000. Under the imprest system, the head cashier reimburses exactly the amount spent, so ₦10,000 is given to restore the float to ₦15,000.
questions.p: Total wey dem spend be 4,200 + 3,100 + 2,700 = ₦10,000. Under imprest system, na the exact amount wey dem spend dem go refund, so dem go give ₦10,000 make float return to ₦15,000.

questions.q: Using the same information as above (Adaeze Ventures: float of ₦15,000; spent ₦4,200 on stationery, ₦3,100 on postage and ₦2,700 on cleaning materials), what is the balance of cash in hand in the petty cash box before the head cashier makes the reimbursement?
questions.e: Total spent = ₦10,000. Balance in hand = Float − Total spent = 15,000 − 10,000 = ₦5,000. This is the amount left before the head cashier tops it back up to ₦15,000.
questions.p: Total wey dem spend na ₦10,000. Balance wey remain = Float minus total spent = 15,000 − 10,000 = ₦5,000. Na this balance dey remain before dem top am back to ₦15,000.

questions.q: In an analytical petty cash book with several expense analysis columns (such as stationery, postage, cleaning and transport), the total of all the analysis columns added together should equal:
o: the opening float for the period
the total of the payments (total) column
the amount reimbursed by the head cashier only
questions.e: Each payment is entered once in the total payments column and once again in its matching analysis column. So when you add up all the analysis columns, the sum must equal the total payments column, which checks the accuracy of the book.
questions.p: Every payment dem go write am once for total column and once again for the matching analysis column. So if you add all the analysis columns, e must balance with total payments column, na so dem dey check say book correct.

questions.q: Chidinma Stores operates the imprest system with a petty cash float of ₦20,000. In the first week, the petty cashier spent ₦8,500 on various small expenses. At the start of the second week, the head cashier decided to increase the float permanently from ₦20,000 to ₦25,000, and gave the petty cashier a single cheque to cover both the normal reimbursement and the increase. How much was this cheque?
questions.e: Normal reimbursement to restore the old float = ₦8,500 (the amount spent). The increase in float = 25,000 − 20,000 = ₦5,000. Total cheque given = 8,500 + 5,000 = ₦13,500.
questions.p: Normal refund wey go restore old float na ₦8,500 (wetin dem spend). The increase for float na 25,000 minus 20,000 = ₦5,000. So total cheque wey dem give na 8,500 + 5,000 = ₦13,500.

questions.q: At the end of the month, the petty cash book of Emeka & Sons showed total analysed payments of ₦9,300 for a float of ₦15,000. However, when the head cashier physically counted the cash in the petty cash box, only ₦5,500 was found. What is the amount of cash shortage?
questions.e: Expected balance in hand = Float − Total payments = 15,000 − 9,300 = ₦5,700. Since only ₦5,500 was physically found, the shortage = 5,700 − 5,500 = ₦200.
questions.p: Balance wey suppose dey hand = Float minus total payments = 15,000 − 9,300 = ₦5,700. But since na ₦5,500 dem see for box, the shortage = 5,700 − 5,500 = ₦200.

questions.q: In the final accounts of a sole trader, the trading account is mainly prepared to determine which of the following?
o: The total capital employed in the business
The financial position of the business
questions.e: The trading account compares sales with the cost of goods sold to find gross profit or gross loss. Net profit is found later in the profit and loss account.
questions.p: Trading account na for compare sales with cost of goods wey dem sell, so e dey show gross profit or gross loss. Na profit and loss account dey show net profit.

questions.q: Chidinma Stores recorded sales of ₦150,000 and cost of sales of ₦90,000 for the year. What is the gross profit?
questions.e: Gross profit = Sales - Cost of sales = ₦150,000 - ₦90,000 = ₦60,000.
questions.p: Gross profit = Sales minus Cost of sales = ₦150,000 - ₦90,000 = ₦60,000.

questions.q: A trader's records show: Opening stock ₦20,000, Purchases ₦80,000, Closing stock ₦15,000. What is the cost of sales for the year?
questions.e: Cost of sales = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock = ₦20,000 + ₦80,000 - ₦15,000 = ₦85,000.
questions.p: Cost of sales = Opening stock + Purchases - Closing stock = ₦20,000 + ₦80,000 - ₦15,000 = ₦85,000.

questions.q: In the final accounts of a sole trader, how is closing stock usually treated?
o: It is shown as a debit in the profit and loss account and a liability in the balance sheet
It is shown as a credit in the profit and loss account and a current liability in the balance sheet
It is shown as a debit in the trading account and a liability in the balance sheet
It is shown as a credit in the trading account and a current asset in the balance sheet
questions.e: Closing stock reduces cost of sales, so it is credited in the trading account, and it also appears as a current asset in the balance sheet since it is goods still unsold.
questions.p: Closing stock dey reduce cost of sales, so dem go credit am for trading account, and e go also appear as current asset for balance sheet because na goods wey never sell.

questions.q: On 1 October, a trader paid ₦36,000 insurance premium covering 12 months from that date. If the trader's financial year ends on 31 December the same year, what amount should be treated as prepaid insurance at year end?
questions.e: Only 3 months (October to December) relate to the current year, leaving 9 months prepaid. Prepaid amount = ₦36,000 x 9/12 = ₦27,000.
questions.p: Na 3 months (October to December) concern this year, so 9 months remain as prepaid. Prepaid = ₦36,000 x 9/12 = ₦27,000.

questions.q: Bisi started the year with a capital of ₦500,000. During the year, she made a net profit of ₦120,000, introduced additional capital of ₦30,000 and made drawings of ₦45,000. What is her closing capital at year end?
questions.e: Closing capital = Opening capital + Net profit + Additional capital - Drawings = ₦500,000 + ₦120,000 + ₦30,000 - ₦45,000 = ₦605,000.
questions.p: Closing capital = Opening capital + Net profit + Extra capital - Drawings = ₦500,000 + ₦120,000 + ₦30,000 - ₦45,000 = ₦605,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes an 'accrued expense' in the preparation of final accounts?
o: An expense that has been incurred but not yet paid for at the end of the accounting period
An expense that has been paid in advance before it becomes due
A debt that has been confirmed as uncollectible and removed from the books
An amount set aside to cover possible future losses on debtors
questions.e: An accrued expense is one that a business has used or enjoyed during the period but has not yet paid for by the year end. It is shown as a current liability in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Accrued expense na expense wey business don use already but e never pay am before year end. Dem go show am as current liability for the statement of financial position.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa paid for business insurance that covers a period extending beyond the end of his accounting year. The portion of the payment relating to the next accounting year should be treated in the final accounts as a...
o: Accrued expense, shown as a current liability
Prepaid expense, shown as a current asset in the statement of financial position
questions.e: Since the payment covers a future period not yet used, the unused part is a prepayment. It is an asset because it represents a benefit still to be enjoyed, so it appears as a current asset.
questions.p: Since the money cover period wey never reach, the part wey remain na prepayment. E be asset because the benefit never finish, so e go show as current asset.

questions.q: Alhaja Bello paid ₦84,000 as rent to cover a full 12-month period from 1st July of the current year to 30th June of the following year. Her accounting year ends on 31st December. Calculate the amount of prepaid rent to be shown in her statement of financial position at 31st December.
questions.e: Monthly rent = 84000/12 = ₦7,000. From July to December (6 months) has been used, so the remaining 6 months (January to June) is prepaid: 6 x 7000 = ₦42,000.
questions.p: Rent for one month = 84000/12 = ₦7,000. From July to December na 6 months wey don pass, so the remaining 6 months (January to June) na prepaid: 6 x 7000 = ₦42,000.

questions.q: Chidinma Ventures had trade receivables (debtors) of ₦500,000 at the end of the financial year. The business maintains a provision for doubtful debts at 5% of trade receivables. Calculate the amount of the provision for doubtful debts.
questions.e: The provision is calculated as 5% of the trade receivables: 5/100 x 500,000 = ₦25,000. This is the amount to be deducted from debtors in the balance sheet and charged against profit.
questions.p: Dem go calculate the provision as 5% of the debtors: 5/100 x 500,000 = ₦25,000. Na dis amount dem go minus from debtors for balance sheet and charge am against profit.

questions.q: A trader had earlier written off a customer's debt of ₦15,000 as a bad debt. Two years later, the customer unexpectedly paid back the full amount. How should this recovered amount be treated in the books?
o: Deducted directly from the trade receivables control account only, with no entry in the profit and loss account
Credited to a bad debts recovered account and then transferred to the profit and loss account as income
Added to the provision for doubtful debts for the year
Treated as a capital reserve in the statement of financial position
questions.e: Since the debt was already written off, the recovery is treated as a gain. It is credited to a bad debts recovered account and later transferred to the profit and loss account as other income.
questions.p: Since dem don already write off the debt before, when e come pay back, na gain. Dem go credit am for bad debts recovered account, later transfer am go profit and loss account as income.

questions.q: Before adjustments, a trader's net profit for the year was ₦250,000. At year end, it was discovered that rent of ₦12,000 had been prepaid (already charged as an expense for a period not yet enjoyed), while wages of ₦18,000 for the last week of the year had not yet been paid or recorded. Calculate the adjusted net profit after making these corrections.
questions.e: The prepaid rent of ₦12,000 was wrongly charged as an expense, so it is added back to profit. The accrued wages of ₦18,000 is an expense not yet recorded, so it is subtracted. Adjusted profit = 250,000 + 12,000 - 18,000 = ₦244,000.
questions.p: Dem don wrongly charge the ₦12,000 prepaid rent as expense, so make dem add am back to profit. The ₦18,000 wages wey dem never record na expense, so make dem minus am. Adjusted profit = 250,000 + 12,000 - 18,000 = ₦244,000.

questions.q: At the start of the year, a business had a provision for doubtful debts of ₦15,000. During the year, trade receivables stood at ₦368,000 before writing off a bad debt of ₦8,000. After writing off the bad debt, the business decided to maintain a provision for doubtful debts of 5% of the remaining net receivables. Calculate the amount to be charged to the profit and loss account specifically for the change in the provision for doubtful debts.
questions.e: Net receivables after writing off bad debts = 368,000 - 8,000 = ₦360,000. New provision = 5% x 360,000 = ₦18,000. Since the opening provision was ₦15,000, the increase charged to the profit and loss account is 18,000 - 15,000 = ₦3,000.
questions.p: Net receivables after dem write off the bad debt = 368,000 - 8,000 = ₦360,000. New provision = 5% x 360,000 = ₦18,000. Since the old provision na ₦15,000, the increase wey dem go charge for profit and loss account na 18,000 - 15,000 = ₦3,000.

questions.q: Which of the following best defines depreciation of a non-current asset in financial accounting?
o: The systematic allocation of the cost of a non-current asset over its useful life
The fall in the market value of an asset caused by inflation
The amount of cash set aside to replace a non-current asset when it wears out
The total amount spent on repairing and maintaining a non-current asset
questions.e: Depreciation is an accounting process that spreads (allocates) the cost of a non-current asset over the years it is expected to be used. It is not cash saved, not a maintenance cost, and not just a market value change.
questions.p: Depreciation na how dem dey share the cost of asset across the years wey e go dey used. E no be money wey dem dey keep aside, e no be repair cost, and e no be market value wahala.

questions.q: Chidi Motors bought a delivery van for ₦1,800,000. The van has an estimated useful life of 8 years and an expected residual (scrap) value of ₦200,000 at the end of its life. Using the straight line method, what is the annual depreciation charge?
questions.e: Straight line depreciation = (Cost - Residual value) / Useful life = (1,800,000 - 200,000) / 8 = 1,600,000 / 8 = ₦200,000 per year.
questions.p: Straight line depreciation = (Cost minus Scrap value) divided by number of years = (1,800,000 - 200,000)/8 = 1,600,000/8 = ₦200,000 every year.

questions.q: A machine costing ₦500,000 is depreciated at 20% per annum using the reducing balance method. What is the net book value of the machine at the end of the second year?
questions.e: Year 1: 500,000 x (1-0.20) = 400,000. Year 2: 400,000 x (1-0.20) = 320,000. The reducing balance method applies the rate to the book value remaining after the previous year's depreciation, not to the original cost.
questions.p: Year 1: 500,000 x 0.80 = 400,000. Year 2: 400,000 x 0.80 = 320,000. For reducing balance, dem dey use the rate on the balance wey remain, no be on the original cost.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a cause of depreciation of a non-current asset?
o: Wear and tear arising from usage
Increase in the market price of the asset due to inflation
questions.e: Depreciation is caused by wear and tear, obsolescence and time passing. A rise in market price due to inflation is not a cause of depreciation; it is actually a form of appreciation, not an accounting depreciation cause.
questions.p: Depreciation dey happen because of wear and tear, old technology, and time wey don pass. If market price rise because of inflation, na appreciation, e no be reason for depreciation.

questions.q: Adaeze Enterprises bought office equipment for ₦960,000 on 1st January 2021. The equipment has an estimated useful life of 6 years with no residual value, and the straight line method is used. The company's financial year ends on 31st December. What is the net book value of the equipment as at 31st December 2023?
questions.e: Annual depreciation = 960,000 / 6 = 160,000. By 31st December 2023, three full years (2021, 2022, 2023) have passed, so accumulated depreciation = 160,000 x 3 = 480,000. Net book value = 960,000 - 480,000 = ₦480,000.
questions.p: Every year depreciation = 960,000 / 6 = 160,000. From 2021 to 2023 na 3 years, so total depreciation = 160,000 x 3 = 480,000. Net book value = 960,000 - 480,000 = ₦480,000.

questions.q: In the books of a business, what is the correct double entry to record the annual depreciation charge on a non-current asset?
o: Debit the provision for depreciation account; Credit the bank account
Debit the depreciation expense account; Credit the provision for depreciation account
Debit the non-current asset account; Credit the depreciation expense account
Debit the bank account; Credit the non-current asset account
questions.e: Depreciation is an expense, so it is debited to the depreciation expense (profit or loss) account, while the accumulated amount is credited to the provision for depreciation account, which reduces the asset's net book value in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Depreciation na expense, so dem go debit depreciation expense account, then credit provision for depreciation account. Na this provision account dey reduce the asset value for statement of financial position.

questions.q: An asset was bought for ₦800,000. After two years of depreciation using the reducing balance method, its net book value is ₦512,000. What annual rate of depreciation was used?
questions.e: Let r be the rate. 800,000 x (1-r)^2 = 512,000, so (1-r)^2 = 512,000/800,000 = 0.64. Taking the square root, 1-r = 0.8, so r = 0.2, which is 20%.
questions.p: Make r be the rate. 800,000 x (1-r)^2 = 512,000, so (1-r)^2 = 0.64. Find square root, 1-r = 0.8, so r = 0.2, wey be 20%.

questions.q: The Sales Ledger Control Account is also commonly known as the:
questions.e: The Sales Ledger Control Account summarises all individual customers' (debtors') accounts, so it is also called the Total Debtors Account.
questions.p: Sales Ledger Control Account dey summarise all the customers (debtors) accounts, so dem dey also call am Total Debtors Account.

questions.q: At the start of the year, Chidinma Stores had total debtors of ₦185,000. During the year, credit sales amounted to ₦940,000, cash received from debtors was ₦820,000, discount allowed was ₦25,000, returns inwards was ₦30,000, and bad debts written off was ₦15,000. What is the closing balance of the Sales Ledger Control Account?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit sales - Cash received - Discount allowed - Returns inwards - Bad debts = 185,000 + 940,000 - 820,000 - 25,000 - 30,000 - 15,000 = ₦235,000.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit sales - Cash wey enter - Discount wey dem allow - Returns inwards - Bad debts = 185,000 + 940,000 - 820,000 - 25,000 - 30,000 - 15,000 = ₦235,000.

questions.q: At the beginning of the year, Obiora Ventures owed creditors a total of ₦150,000. During the year, credit purchases amounted to ₦680,000, cash paid to suppliers was ₦600,000, discount received was ₦20,000, and returns outwards amounted to ₦18,000. What is the closing balance of the Purchases Ledger Control Account?
questions.e: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit purchases - Cash paid - Discount received - Returns outwards = 150,000 + 680,000 - 600,000 - 20,000 - 18,000 = ₦192,000.
questions.p: Closing balance = Opening balance + Credit purchases - Cash wey dem pay - Discount wey dem receive - Returns outwards = 150,000 + 680,000 - 600,000 - 20,000 - 18,000 = ₦192,000.

questions.q: Which of the following items appears on the DEBIT side of the Sales Ledger Control Account?
o: Cheques received from customers that were later dishonoured
Bad debts written off during the year
questions.e: A dishonoured cheque means the customer's debt is restored, so it increases debtors and is debited in the Sales Ledger Control Account. Discount allowed, returns inwards and bad debts all reduce debtors, so they appear on the credit side instead.
questions.p: When cheque bounce (dishonoured), e mean say the customer still owe, so e go increase the debtors and e go dey debit side of Sales Ledger Control Account. Discount allowed, returns inwards and bad debts dey reduce debtors, so dem dey for credit side.

questions.q: Mr. Bassey owes Kalu Enterprises ₦12,000 as a customer, but Kalu Enterprises also owes him ₦12,000 for goods supplied to the business. Both debts are set off (contra entry) against each other in the books. How will this set-off be recorded in the control accounts?
o: Debited in the Sales Ledger Control Account and credited in the Purchases Ledger Control Account
Credited in the Sales Ledger Control Account and debited in the Purchases Ledger Control Account
Debited in both the Sales Ledger Control Account and the Purchases Ledger Control Account
Credited in both the Sales Ledger Control Account and the Purchases Ledger Control Account
questions.e: A contra (set-off) entry reduces both the debtor and creditor balances by the same amount. Since the Sales Ledger Control Account credit side reduces debtors and the Purchases Ledger Control Account debit side reduces creditors, the set-off is credited in the Sales Ledger Control Account and debited in the Purchases Ledger Control Account.
questions.p: Contra entry dey reduce both the debtor and creditor balance with the same amount. Since credit side for Sales Ledger Control Account dey reduce debtors and debit side for Purchases Ledger Control Account dey reduce creditors, dem go credit am for Sales Ledger Control Account and debit am for Purchases Ledger Control Account.

questions.q: A credit sale of ₦5,000 to a customer, Mrs. Adaeze, was completely omitted from the Sales Day Book, the customer's personal account, and the Sales Ledger Control Account. Which of the following statements is correct about this error?
o: It will be revealed immediately when the control account is prepared
It will NOT be revealed by the control account because both the total and the individual accounts are equally affected
It will cause the control account balance to be higher than the total of individual balances
It will cause the control account balance to be lower than the total of individual balances
questions.e: Since the transaction was omitted from every relevant book, both the control account total and the total of individual debtor balances are affected in the same way, so they will still agree. An error of complete omission is one of the errors a control account cannot detect.
questions.p: Since dem forget to record the transaction for every relevant book, both the control account total and the individual debtors' total go dey affected the same way, so dem go still agree. Error of complete omission na one of the errors wey control account no fit catch.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a single entry (incomplete records) system of bookkeeping?
o: A system in which only one aspect of each transaction is recorded regularly, so full double-entry details are often missing
A system in which both the debit and credit aspects of every transaction are recorded in separate ledger accounts
A system used exclusively by limited liability companies for preparing their final accounts
A system in which transactions are recorded only in the cash book and no other books of account are kept
questions.e: Single entry (incomplete records) means the business does not keep a full set of double-entry books. Usually only cash transactions or personal accounts are recorded, so other details are missing. It is not the same as double entry (option B) and is not limited to companies (option C).
questions.p: Single entry be say the business no dey keep full double-entry book. Na only small part of transactions dem dey record, like cash. E no be the same thing as double entry wey record debit and credit together.

questions.q: Mr. Adeyemi, a provision store owner in Ibadan, does not keep a full set of ledger books. He only jots down cash he receives and cash he pays out in a notebook. This method of keeping records is called:
questions.e: Since Mr. Adeyemi only records cash received and paid without a complete set of ledgers, he is using the single entry (incomplete records) system. This is common among small traders who do not employ trained accountants.
questions.p: Since Mr. Adeyemi just dey write the cash wey come in and the cash wey comot without full book, na single entry (incomplete records) im dey use. Na common style for small traders.

questions.q: Chinwe's business had an opening capital of ₦250,000 and a closing capital of ₦320,000 at the end of the year. During the year she withdrew ₦45,000 for personal use and introduced an additional ₦30,000 as new capital. What was her profit for the year, using the statement of affairs (net worth) method?
questions.e: Profit = (Closing capital - Opening capital) + Drawings - Additional capital. This gives (320,000 - 250,000) + 45,000 - 30,000 = 70,000 + 45,000 - 30,000 = ₦85,000. Drawings must be added back and new capital introduced must be deducted because they are not profit.
questions.p: Profit = (Closing capital - Opening capital) + Drawings - New capital wey she bring. So (320,000-250,000)+45,000-30,000 = 70,000+45,000-30,000 = ₦85,000. Na so you go remove new capital and add back drawings.

questions.q: At the close of business, a trader's assets were: Cash ₦15,000, Stock ₦60,000, Trade debtors ₦45,000 and Furniture ₦80,000. His liabilities were: Trade creditors ₦35,000 and a loan ₦20,000. What was his capital at that date, as shown by the statement of affairs?
questions.e: Capital = Total assets - Total liabilities. Total assets = 15,000+60,000+45,000+80,000 = ₦200,000, and total liabilities = 35,000+20,000 = ₦55,000. So capital = 200,000 - 55,000 = ₦145,000.
questions.p: Capital = Total assets minus Total liabilities. Total assets na 15,000+60,000+45,000+80,000 = ₦200,000, total liabilities na 35,000+20,000 = ₦55,000. So capital = 200,000-55,000 = ₦145,000.

questions.q: A trader keeps incomplete records of debtors. At the start of the year, debtors owed him ₦40,000 and at the end of the year they owed ₦55,000. During the year he received ₦180,000 cash from debtors, allowed them ₦5,000 discount and accepted ₦10,000 goods returned (returns inward). What was his total credit sales for the year, using the total debtors account?
questions.e: Credit sales = Cash received + Discount allowed + Returns inward + Closing debtors - Opening debtors. This gives 180,000+5,000+10,000+55,000-40,000 = ₦210,000. All these items pass through the total debtors account on the credit side except opening balance and credit sales.
questions.p: Credit sales = Cash wey enter + Discount wey e give + Returns inward + Closing debtors - Opening debtors. E be 180,000+5,000+10,000+55,000-40,000 = ₦210,000. Na so the total debtors account take balance.

questions.q: A trader's records show: Opening creditors ₦30,000, Closing creditors ₦42,000, Cash paid to creditors ₦150,000, Discount received ₦8,000 and Returns outward ₦6,000. What was the total purchases on credit for the year, using the total creditors account?
questions.e: Purchases = Cash paid + Discount received + Returns outward + Closing creditors - Opening creditors. This is 150,000+8,000+6,000+42,000-30,000 = ₦176,000. Discount received and returns outward reduce what is owed, so they must be added back with the cash paid to find total purchases.
questions.p: Purchases = Cash wey e pay + Discount wey e receive + Returns outward + Closing creditors - Opening creditors. E be 150,000+8,000+6,000+42,000-30,000 = ₦176,000. Discount and returns outward na things wey reduce debt, so you go add dem back.

questions.q: A trader marks up all his goods by 25% on cost before selling them. If his total sales for the year amounted to ₦250,000, what was his cost of goods sold?
questions.e: A 25% mark-up on cost means Sales = Cost x 1.25. So Cost = Sales / 1.25 = 250,000 / 1.25 = ₦200,000. Dividing instead of taking a percentage straight off sales avoids the common error of confusing mark-up with margin.
questions.p: 25% mark-up on cost mean Sales = Cost x 1.25. So Cost = Sales divide by 1.25 = 250,000/1.25 = ₦200,000. No confuse mark-up with margin, na why we divide like this.

questions.q: Not-for-profit organisations such as clubs and societies prepare an account that summarises all cash and bank receipts and payments during a financial year, usually showing the opening and closing cash/bank balances. What is this account called?
questions.e: The Receipts and Payments account is a summary of the cash book of a not-for-profit organisation. It records all cash received and paid during the year, whether capital or revenue in nature.
questions.p: Receipts and Payments account na summary of all the cash wey the club receive and pay out for the year. E be like cash book, e no separate capital and revenue items.

questions.q: In the accounts of a social club, the account that matches the income earned and expenditure incurred during the year (on accrual basis), regardless of when cash was actually received or paid, and shows a surplus or deficit, is called the ______.
questions.e: The Income and Expenditure account is the non-profit equivalent of a trading firm's Profit and Loss account. It is prepared on accrual basis and shows surplus (income > expenditure) or deficit (expenditure > income).
questions.p: Income and Expenditure account na like Profit and Loss account for business wey dey make profit. Dem dey use accrual basis, so e go show surplus or deficit, no be cash basis.

questions.q: At 1st January, Ikeja Social Club had the following: Club building ₦500,000, Furniture and fittings ₦80,000, Cash at bank ₦45,000, and Amount owing to a supplier ₦25,000. What was the club's accumulated fund at 1st January?
questions.e: Accumulated fund = Total assets - Total liabilities = (500,000 + 80,000 + 45,000) - 25,000 = 625,000 - 25,000 = ₦600,000. It is the non-profit equivalent of capital.
questions.p: Accumulated fund = Total assets minus Total liabilities. Assets be 500,000+80,000+45,000=625,000, minus the 25,000 wey dem owe = ₦600,000.

questions.q: A town union received ₦85,000 cash as subscriptions during the year. Subscriptions owing (unpaid) by members stood at ₦12,000 at the start of the year and ₦18,000 at the end of the year. What amount should be recorded as subscription income in the Income and Expenditure account for the year?
questions.e: Subscription income = Cash received - Opening arrears + Closing arrears = 85,000 - 12,000 + 18,000 = ₦91,000. The opening arrears were already earned last year, while closing arrears belong to this year's income.
questions.p: Subscription income = Cash wey dem collect minus the old debt (opening arrears) plus the new debt (closing arrears) = 85,000 - 12,000 + 18,000 = ₦91,000.

questions.q: A sports club's bar recorded the following for the year: Bar sales ₦200,000, Cost of bar goods sold ₦140,000, and Bar running expenses (wages and sundries) ₦20,000. What is the bar profit to be transferred to the Income and Expenditure account?
questions.e: Bar profit = Sales - Cost of goods sold - Bar expenses = 200,000 - 140,000 - 20,000 = ₦40,000. This net bar profit (not the gross profit) is what is transferred to the Income and Expenditure account.
questions.p: Bar profit = Sales minus Cost of goods sold minus Bar expenses = 200,000 - 140,000 - 20,000 = ₦40,000. Na dis net figure dem go carry go the Income and Expenditure account.

questions.q: Lagos Tennis Club received ₦60,000 as a life membership fee from a new member. The club's policy is to spread life membership fees over 5 years as income, since members enjoy benefits over that period. How much should be credited to the Income and Expenditure account for the current year?
questions.e: Since the fee is spread equally over 5 years, the annual amount recognised as income = 60,000 / 5 = ₦12,000. The remaining ₦48,000 stays in the statement of financial position as deferred income (life membership fund) until future years.
questions.p: Since dem dey share the ₦60,000 for 5 years, yearly income = 60,000 ÷ 5 = ₦12,000. The remaining ₦48,000 go stay for balance sheet as deferred income until e reach the following years.

questions.q: A social club's Income and Expenditure account for the year showed the following: Subscriptions ₦150,000, Donations ₦20,000, Bar profit ₦40,000; Salaries ₦60,000, Rent ₦30,000, Printing and stationery ₦15,000, Depreciation ₦10,000. What was the club's surplus for the year?
questions.e: Total income = 150,000 + 20,000 + 40,000 = ₦210,000. Total expenditure = 60,000 + 30,000 + 15,000 + 10,000 = ₦115,000. Surplus = 210,000 - 115,000 = ₦95,000, which is added to the accumulated fund.

questions.q: Prime cost in a manufacturing account consists of which combination of cost elements?
o: Direct materials + Direct labour + Factory overhead
Direct materials + Direct labour + Direct expenses
Direct materials + Factory overhead + Administrative expenses
Direct labour + Factory overhead + Selling expenses
questions.e: Prime cost is the total of all direct costs that can be traced straight to the units produced, that is direct materials, direct labour and direct expenses. Factory overhead is added later to get the production cost, not prime cost.
questions.p: Prime cost na all the direct costs wey dem fit trace straight to the goods wey dem produce - direct material, direct labour and direct expenses. Factory overhead no dey inside prime cost, e dey added later to find production cost.

questions.q: Which of the following items would NOT be classified as part of factory overhead in a manufacturing account?
o: Rent and rates on the factory building
Carriage inwards on raw materials purchased
questions.e: Carriage inwards on raw materials is added to the cost of purchases to find the cost of materials consumed, so it is a direct material cost, not factory overhead. Rent, machinery depreciation and supervisor's salary are all indirect factory costs.
questions.p: Carriage inwards on raw material na direct material cost, e dey added to purchases to find cost of material wey dem use - e no be factory overhead. But rent, machine depreciation and supervisor salary na indirect factory cost, so dem be overhead.

questions.q: Adaeze Ventures, a furniture manufacturer in Onitsha, provided the following data for the year: Opening stock of raw materials ₦25,000; Purchases of raw materials ₦180,000; Carriage inwards on raw materials ₦5,000; Closing stock of raw materials ₦30,000. Calculate the cost of raw materials consumed.
questions.e: Cost of raw materials consumed = Opening stock + Purchases + Carriage inwards - Closing stock = 25,000 + 180,000 + 5,000 - 30,000 = ₦180,000.
questions.p: Cost of raw material wey dem use = Opening stock + Purchases + Carriage inwards - Closing stock = 25,000 + 180,000 + 5,000 - 30,000 = ₦180,000.

questions.q: Blessing Manufacturing Company provided the following for the year: Cost of raw materials consumed ₦180,000; Direct labour ₦120,000; Direct expenses ₦15,000. Calculate the prime cost.
questions.e: Prime cost = Direct materials + Direct labour + Direct expenses = 180,000 + 120,000 + 15,000 = ₦315,000.
questions.p: Prime cost = Direct material + Direct labour + Direct expenses = 180,000 + 120,000 + 15,000 = ₦315,000.

questions.q: Chukwuma Industries recorded the following for the year: Prime cost ₦315,000; Factory overhead ₦85,000; Opening work-in-progress ₦20,000; Closing work-in-progress ₦35,000. Calculate the cost of production (cost of goods manufactured).
questions.e: Cost of production = Prime cost + Factory overhead + Opening WIP - Closing WIP = 315,000 + 85,000 + 20,000 - 35,000 = ₦385,000. The opening WIP is added because it joins current production, while closing WIP is removed because it is not yet finished.
questions.p: Cost of production = Prime cost + Factory overhead + Opening WIP - Closing WIP = 315,000 + 85,000 + 20,000 - 35,000 = ₦385,000. Dem add opening WIP because e dey join current production, dem remove closing WIP because e no don finish.

questions.q: Okafor Plastics transferred its finished goods from the factory to the trading account at a transfer price of ₦440,000, representing the market value of the goods produced. If the cost of production for the year was ₦385,000, what is the manufacturing profit for the year?
questions.e: Manufacturing profit = Market (transfer) value - Cost of production = 440,000 - 385,000 = ₦55,000. This profit shows how much the factory would have earned if it sold the goods to an outside buyer instead of its own trading section.
questions.p: Manufacturing profit = Market value (transfer price) - Cost of production = 440,000 - 385,000 = ₦55,000. Na the profit wey the factory for don make if e sell the goods to outside person instead of im own trading section.

questions.q: A shoe manufacturing company in Aba pays a royalty of ₦2 per pair of shoes produced to the patent holder of a special sole design used in production. How should this royalty payment be classified in the manufacturing account?
questions.e: Since the royalty is paid based on the number of units produced, it can be directly traced to the goods manufactured, making it a direct expense that forms part of prime cost.
questions.p: Since dem dey pay the royalty based on number of shoes wey dem produce, e dey directly connect to the goods wey dem make, so e be direct expense wey dey inside prime cost.

questions.q: In a partnership business, which document contains the agreed terms such as capital contribution, profit-sharing ratio, and duties of partners?
questions.e: A partnership deed is the written agreement that states how the partners will run the business, including capital and profit-sharing terms. It is the main legal document guiding the partnership.
questions.p: Partnership deed na di paper wey dem write down di agreement of di partners, like how dem go share profit and wetin each one go contribute. E be like di guiding rulebook for di business.

questions.q: Chika and Dayo formed a partnership but did not sign any partnership agreement. In the absence of such an agreement, how should profits and losses be shared according to general partnership principles?
o: According to age of the partners
questions.e: Where there is no partnership agreement, the law assumes partners share profits and losses equally, regardless of their capital contributions. This is a default rule to avoid disputes.
questions.p: If partners no sign any agreement, di law say make dem share profit and loss equally. E no matter di money wey each one bring come di business.

questions.q: Musa and Ibrahim are partners with capital balances of ₦200,000 and ₦150,000 respectively. Their partnership agreement allows interest on capital at 10% per annum. What is the total interest on capital for the year for both partners?
questions.e: Interest on Musa's capital = 10% of ₦200,000 = ₦20,000. Interest on Ibrahim's capital = 10% of ₦150,000 = ₦15,000. Total interest on capital = ₦20,000 + ₦15,000 = ₦35,000.
questions.p: Musa get 10% of 200,000 wey be 20,000. Ibrahim get 10% of 150,000 wey be 15,000. If you add dem togeda, na 35,000 be di total interest on capital.

questions.q: A partner, Grace, withdrew ₦40,000 from the business at the start of the year. The partnership deed charges interest on drawings at 5% per annum for the full year. How much interest on drawings should be charged to Grace?
questions.e: Interest on drawings = 5% of ₦40,000 = ₦2,000. Since the withdrawal was at the start of the year, the full rate applies for the whole year.
questions.p: Interest on drawings na 5% of 40,000, wey be 2,000. Since na from beginning of year she comot di money, full interest go apply for di whole year.

questions.q: Chidi and Emeka are partners sharing profits and losses in the ratio 3:2. The partnership deed grants Chidi an annual salary of ₦30,000 before profit distribution. The net profit for the year, before any appropriation, is ₦150,000. What is Chidi's total share (salary plus profit share) for the year?
questions.e: First deduct Chidi's salary: ₦150,000 - ₦30,000 = ₦120,000 remaining profit. Chidi's share of this is 3/5 x ₦120,000 = ₦72,000. Adding the salary, Chidi's total = ₦72,000 + ₦30,000 = ₦102,000.
questions.p: First remove Chidi salary from profit: 150,000 minus 30,000 be 120,000. Chidi own share na 3/5 of 120,000 wey be 72,000. Add di salary 30,000, e go be 102,000 total.

questions.q: Tunde and Yusuf are partners with capitals of ₦300,000 and ₦200,000 respectively, earning interest on capital at 5% per annum. Yusuf also receives an annual salary of ₦20,000. The net profit for the year is ₦150,000, and the remaining profit after these appropriations is shared in the ratio 3:2 between Tunde and Yusuf. What is Tunde's total share of the profit for the year?
questions.e: Interest on capital: Tunde = 5% of 300,000 = ₦15,000, Yusuf = 5% of 200,000 = ₦10,000, total ₦25,000. Subtract this and Yusuf's salary (₦20,000) from ₦150,000, leaving ₦105,000 to share 3:2. Tunde's share = 3/5 x 105,000 = ₦63,000, plus his interest on capital ₦15,000 gives ₦78,000.
questions.p: Tunde interest na 5% of 300,000 wey be 15,000, Yusuf own na 10,000, total 25,000. Remove dis 25,000 and Yusuf salary 20,000 from 150,000, remain 105,000 wey dem go share 3:2. Tunde share na 3/5 of 105,000 wey be 63,000, add im interest 15,000, e go be 78,000.

questions.q: Ada and Obi are existing partners sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. A new partner, Ngozi, is admitted and acquires a 1/5 share of future profits, taken equally from Ada and Obi. The goodwill of the firm is valued at ₦120,000, and Ngozi is to pay goodwill for the share she acquires. How much goodwill should Ada receive from Ngozi?
questions.e: Ngozi is acquiring 1/5 of the total goodwill value: 1/5 x ₦120,000 = ₦24,000. Since this 1/5 share is taken equally from Ada and Obi, each receives half of ₦24,000, which is ₦12,000.
questions.p: Ngozi dey take 1/5 share, so goodwill wey she go pay na 1/5 of 120,000 wey be 24,000. Since dem take am equally from Ada and Obi, each one go collect half, wey be 12,000.

questions.q: In company accounts, what term describes the maximum amount of share capital that a company is permitted to issue, as stated in its memorandum of association?
questions.e: Authorised (nominal) share capital is the ceiling amount a company is legally allowed to issue. The company may issue less than this amount at any time.
questions.p: Authorised share capital na the highest amount wey company fit issue as share, as e dey written for the memorandum. Company fit issue less pass this amount.

questions.q: Which group of shareholders is entitled to receive a fixed rate of dividend before any dividend is paid to ordinary shareholders?
questions.e: Preference shareholders get a fixed percentage dividend first, ahead of ordinary shareholders, because of the preferential right attached to their shares.
questions.p: Preference shareholders na the one wey dey collect fixed dividend first before ordinary shareholders, because their shares get special preference.

questions.q: Kaduna Plastics Plc issued 50,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each at ₦1.20 per share. What amount should be credited to the Share Premium Account?
questions.e: Premium per share = ₦1.20 - ₦1.00 = ₦0.20. Total premium = 50,000 x ₦0.20 = ₦10,000, which is transferred to the Share Premium Account.
questions.p: Premium for one share na ₦1.20 minus ₦1.00 wey be ₦0.20. Multiply am by 50,000 shares, e go give ₦10,000 wey dem go put for Share Premium Account.

questions.q: Benue Foods Plc has an issued ordinary share capital of ₦200,000 made up of shares of ₦1 each. The directors declare a dividend of 15%. What is the total dividend payable to the ordinary shareholders?
questions.e: Dividend payable = 15% of ₦200,000 = 0.15 x 200,000 = ₦30,000. Dividend is always calculated on the issued share capital, not authorised capital.
questions.p: Dividend wey go pay na 15% of ₦200,000, wey be 0.15 x 200,000 = ₦30,000. Na issued share capital dem dey use calculate dividend, no be authorised capital.

questions.q: A document issued by a limited liability company acknowledging a loan received, and on which a fixed rate of interest is paid whether the company makes profit or loss, is called a:
questions.e: A debenture is a loan capital instrument; debenture holders are creditors, not owners, and must be paid fixed interest regardless of profit.
questions.p: Debenture na loan document wey company dey give, and debenture holder go always collect fixed interest whether company make profit or loss, because dem be creditor, no be owner.

questions.q: Chinedu was allotted 1,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each, payable ₦0.25 on application, ₦0.25 on allotment and ₦0.50 on first and final call. He paid the application and allotment money but failed to pay the call money, so his shares were forfeited. What amount was already received from Chinedu before the shares were forfeited?
questions.e: Amount received = application (₦0.25 x 1,000) + allotment (₦0.25 x 1,000) = ₦250 + ₦250 = ₦500. The ₦0.50 call was never paid, so it is excluded.
questions.p: Wetin Chinedu don pay na application (₦0.25 x 1,000) plus allotment (₦0.25 x 1,000) = ₦250 + ₦250 = ₦500. E no pay the ₦0.50 call, so dem no go count am.

questions.q: Okoye Industries Plc issued 100,000 ordinary shares of ₦1 each, fully called up. At year end, the holders of 5,000 shares had not paid the final call of ₦0.30 per share. What is the total amount of calls in arrears?
questions.e: Calls in arrears = number of shares in default x unpaid call per share = 5,000 x ₦0.30 = ₦1,500. This amount is deducted from called-up capital in the statement of financial position.
questions.p: Calls in arrears na the shares wey dem never pay multiply by the unpaid amount: 5,000 x ₦0.30 = ₦1,500. Dem go minus this amount from the called-up capital for the statement of financial position.

questions.q: In public sector accounting, which arm of government is constitutionally responsible for approving (appropriating) funds before they can be spent by government ministries?
questions.e: The Legislature (National or State Assembly) passes the Appropriation Act which gives legal backing for government to spend public funds. Without this approval, ministries cannot legally spend money.
questions.p: Na the Legislature (National or State Assembly) dey pass di Appropriation Act wey give government power to spend money. Without dis approval, ministries no fit spend government money legally.

questions.q: Historically, the major source of revenue to the Federal Government of Nigeria has been:
questions.e: Nigeria is a major oil-producing country, and petroleum revenue (crude oil sales and royalties) has traditionally formed the largest share of Federal Government income compared to other listed taxes.
questions.p: Nigeria na big oil-producing country, so money wey dem dey get from petrol (crude oil sales and royalties) don dey bigger pass di oda taxes wey dem list.

questions.q: Which of the following best describes public sector accounting?
o: The process of recording and reporting financial transactions of private companies for shareholders
The preparation of accounts solely to determine profit for distribution to owners
The recording of personal financial transactions of government officials
The process of recording, classifying and reporting financial transactions of government and its agencies to show accountability to the public
questions.e: Public sector accounting deals with how government bodies record, classify and report their financial transactions in order to show stewardship and accountability to the citizens, not to make or share profit.
questions.p: Public sector accounting na how government and im agencies dey record, classify and report dia money matter so dem go fit show say dem dey accountable to di citizens, e no be about profit sharing.

questions.q: Obudu Local Government Council had recurrent revenue of ₦45,000,000 and recurrent expenditure of ₦38,500,000 in one financial year. What was the result on the recurrent account?
questions.e: Recurrent account balance = Recurrent revenue minus Recurrent expenditure = 45,000,000 - 38,500,000 = ₦6,500,000. Since revenue is more than expenditure, it is a surplus.
questions.p: Recurrent account balance = Recurrent revenue minus Recurrent expenditure = 45,000,000 - 38,500,000 = ₦6,500,000. Since revenue pass expenditure, na surplus be dat.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a feature that distinguishes public sector accounting from private sector accounting?
o: Use of fund accounting for different government activities
Accountability of public officers to the citizens
The primary objective of making profit for owners
Strong emphasis on compliance with approved budgets
questions.e: Public sector bodies exist to render services to the public, not to make profit for owners; profit motive is a feature of private sector accounting, so it does not distinguish public sector accounting.
questions.p: Government bodies dey work to serve public, no be to make profit for owners; profit motive na private sector business ting, so e no be feature wey separate public sector accounting.

questions.q: During a financial year, the Federal Government's Consolidated Revenue Fund recorded the following inflows: Taxation ₦120,000,000, Mining rents and royalties ₦45,000,000, Fines and fees ₦5,000,000, and External Loans received ₦30,000,000. Since loans are liabilities and not true revenue, calculate the actual revenue of the government for the year.
questions.e: Actual revenue excludes loans because loans must be repaid and are not earned income. Actual revenue = 120,000,000 + 45,000,000 + 5,000,000 = ₦170,000,000.
questions.p: Real revenue no include loan because loan na debt wey dem go still pay back, e no be money wey dem earn. Real revenue = 120,000,000 + 45,000,000 + 5,000,000 = ₦170,000,000.

questions.q: The document used by a government spending officer to keep a day-to-day record of the budget allocation released to a department, amounts spent, and the balance still available for spending, is called the:
questions.e: The Vote Book is a control record kept by spending officers to track releases, commitments and balances against each budget head, helping to prevent overspending. The Cash Book records actual cash received and paid, while the Appropriation Act only authorises the budget.
questions.p: Vote Book na di book wey spending officer dey use track how much dem release, how much dem spend, and how much remain for each budget head, so dem no go spend pass wetin dem approve. Cash Book na for actual cash wey enter and comot, while Appropriation Act na im dey approve di budget first.

questions.q: In financial accounting, which ratio best measures a business's ability to settle its short-term debts as they fall due?
questions.e: The current ratio compares current assets to current liabilities, showing if a business can pay its short-term debts. The other ratios measure profitability, not liquidity.
questions.p: Current ratio na im dem dey use check if business fit pay im short-term debt. Di oda ones na for profit, dem no dey show liquidity.

questions.q: Which formula correctly gives the gross profit margin of a business?
questions.e: Gross profit margin is calculated by dividing gross profit by sales and multiplying by 100 to express it as a percentage. This shows how much profit is made on sales before other expenses.
questions.p: Gross profit margin na when you divide gross profit by sales multiply by 100. E dey show how much profit dem make before oda expenses.

questions.q: Alhaji Musa's business has current assets of ₦180,000 and current liabilities of ₦90,000 as at 31st December. What is the current ratio?
questions.e: Current ratio = Current assets ÷ Current liabilities = ₦180,000 ÷ ₦90,000 = 2:1. This means the business has ₦2 of current assets for every ₦1 of current liabilities.
questions.p: Current ratio = Current assets divide by Current liabilities = 180,000 divide by 90,000 = 2:1. E mean say business get ₦2 current asset for every ₦1 current liability.

questions.q: Chidinma Enterprises recorded sales of ₦500,000 and cost of sales of ₦350,000 for the year. What is the gross profit margin?
questions.e: Gross profit = Sales - Cost of sales = ₦500,000 - ₦350,000 = ₦150,000. Gross profit margin = (150,000 / 500,000) x 100 = 30%.
questions.p: Gross profit = Sales minus Cost of sales = 500,000 - 350,000 = 150,000. Gross profit margin = (150,000/500,000) x 100 = 30%.

questions.q: A trader's statement of financial position shows current assets of ₦240,000, which includes closing stock of ₦60,000, and current liabilities of ₦120,000. What is the acid test (quick) ratio?
questions.e: Quick assets = Current assets - Stock = ₦240,000 - ₦60,000 = ₦180,000. Acid test ratio = 180,000 ÷ 120,000 = 1.5:1, since stock is excluded for being less liquid.
questions.p: Quick assets = Current assets minus Stock = 240,000 - 60,000 = 180,000. Acid test ratio = 180,000 divide by 120,000 = 1.5:1, because stock no too liquid so dem remove am.

questions.q: Okafor and Sons made a net profit of ₦80,000 on a capital employed of ₦400,000 during the year. What is the return on capital employed (ROCE)?
questions.e: ROCE = (Net profit / Capital employed) x 100 = (80,000 / 400,000) x 100 = 20%. This shows how efficiently the capital invested in the business is generating profit.
questions.p: ROCE = (Net profit divide by Capital employed) x 100 = (80,000/400,000) x 100 = 20%. E dey show how di money wey dem put for business dey work well to bring profit.

questions.q: A supermarket had an average stock of ₦50,000 and a cost of sales of ₦400,000 for the year. How many times did the stock turn over during the year?
questions.e: Rate of stock turnover = Cost of sales / Average stock = ₦400,000 / ₦50,000 = 8 times. This means the business sold and replaced its stock 8 times during the year.
questions.p: Rate of stock turnover = Cost of sales divide by Average stock = 400,000/50,000 = 8 times. E mean say business sell and replace im stock 8 times for that year.
